::: {.why}
Order selection by information criterion is a machine's answer; being able to look at two plots and say AR(2) is what makes you useful in a meeting, and it takes one sitting to learn.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Given an ACF and PACF pair, name the model order and say which of the two plots carried the information.
- Say what the confidence bands on an ACF plot assume, and why they are too narrow for a return series.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build the identification table for yourself: simulate AR(1), AR(2), MA(1), MA(2) and ARMA(1,1) with 2,000 observations each, plot ACF and PACF for all five, and write down which plot cuts off and which tails off in each case. Keep the figure; it is the reference you will use rather than a textbook table.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Test yourself blind: have a script generate one of the five at random with an unseen seed, plot only the two functions, and write down your call before revealing the answer. Ten trials. Record your hit rate.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Derive why the standard confidence band is the reciprocal of the square root of the sample size, and say what happens to it when the series has conditional heteroskedasticity.
:::
:::

## Resources

- [Hyndman & Athanasopoulos — Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd ed.](https://otexts.com/fpp3/) [textbook]{.res-kind}
- [statsmodels — time series analysis (tsa)](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/tsa.html) [tool]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
The five-model ACF and PACF identification figure, plus your hit rate over ten blind trials.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
The PACF cuts off after lag 2 and the ACF decays geometrically. What model is it, and how would the answer look if it were the other way round?
:::
